newsitem.title: USA: S&P AFFIRMS PROFESSIONALS INSURANCE UNIT.
newsitem.headline: S&P AFFIRMS PROFESSIONALS INSURANCE UNIT.

text.p: NEW YORK, Aug 15 - Standard & Poor's today affirmed its triple-B'-plus claims-paying ability and counterparty credit ratings of Michigan-based PICOM Insurance Co. and PICOM Insurance Co. of IL, collectively known as the PICOM Insurance Group (PICOM).

The affirmation follows the announcement that PICOM's public parent, Professionals Insurance Co. Management Group, has signed a definitive agreement to merge PICOM Insurance Co. with Physicians Protective Trust Fund (PPTF) of Coral Gables, Fla.
Pursuant to the terms of the agreement, Professionals Group will issue shares of common stock to eligible members of PPTF in exchange for the assets and liabilities of PPTF.
PPTF is a Florida trust that was organized in 1975 to provide direct medical malpractice liability insurance to physicians located in Florida.
As of Dec. 31, 1996, PPTF wrote $69 million in premiums with statutory surplus of $105 million and invested assets of $343 million.
Standard & Poor's believes the transaction is consistent with management's stated objective, which is to improve the business position of the company through acquisition opportunities.
Pending regulatory approval, Standard & Poor's expects the transaction to substantially increase statutory surplus to approximately $185 million from $81 million.

The quality and strength of capitalization is expected to remain supportive of PICOM's rating, with a Standard & Poor's capital adequacy ratio above 250%. Similarly, profit margins are expected to remain strong although slightly weaker as PICOM needs to address potential loss reserve deficiencies on the acquired book of business.
However, Standard & Poor's believes PICOM's earnings could eventually benefit from a more diversified book of business.
Historically, PICOM derived more than 85% of its premiums and earnings from writing medical malpractice insurance coverages in Michigan.
Post transaction, Standard & Poor's expects writings in Michigan to account for less than 50% of total writings. -- CreditWire
The outlook is based on Standard & Poor's opinion that earnings and capitalization will remain supportive of the rating. Friday, 15 August 1997 16:11:55 ENDS nN15284206
